matchups.analysis: Rob's got 32% and a 13.3-point projection hole (91.6 to 94.7) with only Kyren Williams left to play, which means Adam's already basically got this wrapped up before the second half even finishes—ESPN doesn't hand out 68% win probability odds for fun. The real killer is that you benched Rachaad White for 11.3 points to start Jadarian Price, who promptly shit the bed with 4.5, and that 6.8-point swing is exactly the kind of self-inflicted wound that turns a close game into a coronation for the other guy. Adam's already cashed with Patrick Mahomes going absolutely nuclear (29.0 when ESPN said 18.2), so even Justin Jefferson's stinker (7.0 on a 15.0 projection) doesn't matter because the scoreboard's already written—Kyren Williams would need to go full Superman just to make this respectable, and we both know that's not happening.

Rilind's walking out of this one with 67% win probability and a 3.1-point projection edge that ESPN's basically already penciled in as done—Rinor's sitting at 33% and needs Davante Adams to go full ceiling mode while somehow erasing the fact that he benched Tre Tucker for a -0.1 performance from DJ Moore, a decision that cost him 20.5 points and turned what could've been competitive into a near-certain loss. Davante's got maybe 12-15 points of projection runway left, Rilind's already got the safer floor built on Amon-Ra St. Brown embarrassing his own projection by 14 points, and the math doesn't work in your favor when your only remaining starter has to carry the entire team while your brother's depth just needs to function normally. You had the talent to win this and instead you're explaining to the family next Thanksgiving why you benched a guy who scored 20 while starting a guy who scored negative, which is the kind of self-inflicted wound that stays funny for years—Rilind gets all the bragging rights without even having to work for it.

Flamur's walking out of this one with 97.8 and ESPN's got him at 97% to win with Isaiah Likely still waiting in the wings—but let's be honest, CeeDee Lamb dropping 31.3 when he was only supposed to get 14.9 basically already wrapped this up before halftime even finished. Jetmir and Peter are completely cooked at 98.6 with nothing left to play and a 3% prayer, which is what happens when you bench a guy who scores 6.7 (Malik Washington) to start someone who gives you 3.1 (Rhamondre Stevenson)—that's a 3.6-point swing that turned a coinflip into a funeral. Caleb Williams turned into absolute dogshit with 7.7 points against a 19.4 projection, so between the bench miscalculation and your QB imploding, you're looking at a combined 10+ point disaster that nobody's coming back from down this late.

Arben's walking away with this one at 100% win probability with all starters already in the books—ESPN's got the coffin nailed shut and Ilir's staring at the ash heap with zero percent and no second chances left. Ilir got absolutely murdered by the Bijan Robinson decision (9.6 points when he was supposed to get 20.4) and then compounded it by benching Jonah Coleman for David Montgomery, which cost him nearly 10 points combined—that's 9.9 points of pure self-inflicted damage that turned a close game into a mercy killing before halftime. Josh Allen carried Ilir's corpse with 40.8 points, but one studs' ceiling performance can't save you when you're actively sabotaging yourself in the flex spot and your running back lottery tickets blow up in your face. Arben lucked into JSN going bonkers for 38 points (his projected 15.2 means he basically got a free 23-point gift from the universe), and even though he wasted 4.9 points by benching Ferguson for Hubbard, Lamar's underperformance and all his other mid-range contributions just needed to not completely crater—which they didn't. Arben's taking this home clean while Ilir's left explaining why he had two separate lineup mistakes that each cost him nearly 5 and 10 points respectively.

Nori's walking in at 91% and ESPN's basically already handed him the trophy—73.1 now with a projected 91.3 finish means Faton would need to will himself to 109.3 on pure spite while Nori just needs Jaxson Dart to not actively sabotage things, and that's not a realistic ask when you're already staring down an 18-point hole. Faton's got nothing left to play and still somehow managed to bench Rashod Bateman (18.3 points) in favor of starting J.K. Dobbins (3.6 points) like he was playing 4D chess against himself—that 14.7-point self-inflicted wound would've made this competitive, instead it's the exact reason this matchup's already over. Javonte Williams underperforming by 9.1 points is background noise for Nori when you've spent all week making the kind of roster decisions that guarantee you finish third instead of second, and Colston Loveland's 0.8 points just adds insult to a decision-making process that was already fully broken before Sunday even started.

Ben's walking in with 98% win probability and a 17-point projection cushion (102.8 to 85.7), which means ESPN's basically already mailed in the trophy before Veton's even finished his first drive—but here's the thing: Ben didn't get here by being competent, he got here by having Travis Kelce absolutely lose his mind and drop 20.6 points when the projection said 8.4, which is the kind of ceiling performance you can't plan for. Veton's sitting at 2% because he managed the rare feat of completely fucking up a winnable week—benching Brock Purdy (28.5 points) to start Jalen Hurts (16.2) is the kind of lineup move that costs you 12+ points and basically forfeits the game before kickoff, and that's before we even talk about Dallas Goedert laying a complete egg with 0.9 when ESPN projected 8.6. Ben's still got Cam Skattebo left to play so he's not quite coasting, but between Ladd McConkey underperforming by 7 points and your entire team basically needing a synchronized miracle to catch up, Veton's out here trying to make Malik Nabers carry a corpse of a roster across the finish line—and that's not how this ends.
